cands.bio: Republican from Randolph, NJ. Yale political science graduate (2009). Worked as an advance aide to Gov. Chris Christie, then in corporate affairs and communications in healthcare and financial services. Randolph Township Council member since May 2022 and mayor in 2025.
cands.gaps: We found no documented stance from Hathaway on data centers or on development and land-use limits. We found no record of how he voted on the Randolph Township Council, so we can't show specific votes or official actions on the issues voters care about. His campaign site credits him with negotiating Randolph's affordable housing settlement and with other township results, but we found no independent record confirming these, so we left them out. We found no statements from him on guns, abortion, school choice or teacher pay, H-1B visas, or foreign real-estate buyers. We found no notable endorsements, since Ballotpedia lists none, and no controversies. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. The campaign website's platform page was cut off partway through the healthcare section, so later sections were read only through Ballotpedia's copy of the platform.

cands.bio: Democratic U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 11th District since April 2026. Born and raised in Elizabeth. Former union organizer, director of the NJ Working Families Alliance, national political director for Bernie Sanders' 2020 campaign, deputy director of the U.S. Labor Department's Women's Bureau, and co-executive director of the Center for Popular Democracy.

endorsements.text: Sen. Bernie Sanders, Sen. Elizabeth Warren, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Newark Mayor Ras Baraka, and the New Jersey Working Families Party endorsed her in the 2026 special election. Working Families Party, Emgage Action and New Jersey Citizen Action endorsed her in the regular election.

cands.gaps: We found no record of actions taken in office, so there is nothing yet showing what she has done as a member of Congress. We found nothing on her positions on homestead property taxes, growth and land conservation, policing and public safety, gun laws, school choice or teacher pay, or H-1B visas. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no documented statements from her on development, apart from data centers. Her birth year comes from Wikipedia only.

stop-data-centers.evidence: Her campaign website said she would co-sponsor Sen. Bernie Sanders' moratorium on new AI data centers and make Big Tech pay for the energy it uses.

land-for-floridians.evidence: Her campaign website said she would pass a ban on hedge funds and private equity buying homes, and champion the Homes for All Act.

clean-money.evidence: Her campaign website said she supports a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United and publicly financed elections to limit big-money influence.

workers-first.evidence: She has called for abolishing ICE, and her campaign site promoted an 'Abolish ICE' message.
